summary: Coastal aquifer, Ashdod to Haifa. In boreholes the fresh/saline interface in the calcareous sandstone matches, in most places, the 25 ohm.m contour of measured (apparent) resistivity; the contact is irregular, not parabolic as in the hydrological models. In the interpreted sections the lowest horizon has calculated resistivities of 3.5-7.5 ohm.m (low) and 0-3.5 ohm.m (minimal), matching the salinity of the interface zone; dry sand at the top has 210-850 ohm.m. Measured resistivity maxima are 100-150 ohm.m and minima 5-25 ohm.m; section maxima 375-1900 ohm.m sit at shallow depth and minima of 2.5-50 ohm.m at depth and near the sea.

provenance.notes: Read from the Hebrew text (sections 4.3 and 5.0). The maps and sections it cites are in atlas volumes A, B and D, which are not in the collection.

notes: Useful as an interpretation rule: apparent resistivity below about 25 ohm.m marks saline water in the coastal aquifer.

provenance.notes: Strip positions are on atlas volume A maps, not in the collection, so no sites are attached.
